hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A visual representation of a user or entity, shown as a photo, initials, or icon, with an optional status indicator. Available in nine sizes, from xxxsmall to xxxlarge. Content type isn't an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it. For a notification count on an icon or nav item, use the Notification Indicator component instead, Avatar's own indicator is for presence, not counts.

rows.Description: 24×24px, the smallest size, for dense inline contexts like compact tables or comment threads.
32×32px, a step up from xxxsmall, still compact, for dense lists.
36×36px, for secondary avatars in tight layouts, like a stacked group of collaborators.
40×40px, for list rows and menu items where the avatar sits alongside text.
48×48px, a balanced, general-purpose choice for cards and list headers.
64×64px, for emphasis in a card header or a comment's author avatar.
80×80px, for a prominent single avatar, like a user menu or account switcher.
120×120px, for profile headers where the avatar is a focal point.
200×200px, the largest size, for full profile pages or standalone display contexts.
Shows a dismiss badge pinned to the top-right corner. Use in removable contexts, like a multi-select chip list.
Hides the dismiss badge. The default for most read-only contexts where the avatar isn't removable.
Shows a presence badge pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaults to Available. Swap the nested Status instance to show a different presence state, it isn't an exposed property.
Hides the presence badge. Use when presence doesn't apply, like a generic entity avatar or a purely illustrative photo.
Shows a border/default outline ring around the avatar, weight scales with Size.
Hides the ring. Use on backgrounds where the outline competes with surrounding content.

rows.What changes: Avatar has no hover, pressed, or focus states in Figma. Close and Status are static badges, whatever click behavior Close has in a real interface lives in code, not modeled here.

rows.Description: None modeled in Figma. Avatar is presented as a static graphic, any transition when swapping Size, content, or toggling Show Close, Show Status, or Show Ring lives in code.
Initials, photo, or icon. Not an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it.
Background color behind initials or an icon (purple, blue, sea, yellow, orange, green, burgundy, using chart/series tokens). Not used behind a photo. Swap the nested Swatch instance directly.
Used only when Content type is photo, fills the circle. Swap the nested Photo instance to any of the named photos in _Avatar Photos.
Available (default), Away, Busy, DND, On Shift, or Offline. Not an exposed property, swap the nested Status instance directly. Only shown when Show Status is true.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: Fills the frame, auto-positioned. Holds initials with a colored swatch, a photo, or an icon with a colored swatch. Not an exposed property, swap the nested instance directly
An absolute-positioned outline matching the frame's edges. border/default color, stroke only. Weight scales with Size, 2px from xxxsmall to medium up to 8px at xxxlarge
Pinned to the top-right corner. An instance of the Status Indicator component's Close variant, shown or hidden with Show Close
Pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaults to Available. Shown or hidden with Show Status, swap the nested instance to change the presence state

sections.title: How to use
dos: Match Size to context, dense lists and tables call for the smaller sizes (xxxsmall to small), profile headers and standalone display call for the larger ones (xlarge to xxxlarge).
Turn off Show Status for generic entities or purely illustrative photos where presence doesn't apply.
donts: Don't use the presence Status badge for unread or notification counts, that's a different purpose, use the Notification Indicator component instead.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: Purely visual, an avatar image or initials alone don't convey a name, pair it with visible text or provide an accessible name in code
The Status presence badge is color-only (Available, Away, Busy, DND, On Shift, Offline), pair it with a text label or tooltip in code so presence isn't conveyed by color alone
The Close badge implies a dismiss action, give it an accessible name in code like "Remove [name]", Figma has no interactive state for it

rows.Description: Always a fixed square, 24px to 200px across nine steps, not resizable independent of the Size property.
2px (stroke/thick) from xxxsmall to medium, 4px (stroke/heavy) at large and xlarge, 6px and 8px (not bound to a token) at xxlarge and xxxlarge.
Pinned to the top-right and bottom-right corners respectively via corner constraints. They scale in position as the avatar resizes but don't move independently.
Ring uses border/default. Status and Swatch colors use chart/series, chart/positive, and chart/negative tokens. All resolve separately for light and dark mode.
